tool.jwt.description: Decode, verify, forge (alg none / HS256) and crack the secret of a JSON Web Token, offline.
tool.jwt.error.badChar: Not a clean JWT: unexpected character "{char}". Base64URL only uses A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ and dots.
tool.jwt.error.cannotSign: Cannot sign with "{alg}" here. Use none, HS256, HS384 or HS512.
tool.jwt.error.certificate: That is a certificate, not a bare key. Extract the key with: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -pubkey -noout
tool.jwt.error.headerNotB64: The header is not Base64URL ({reason}) Was the token cut short?
tool.jwt.error.headerNotJson: The header (first part) is not JSON. Is this really a JWT?
tool.jwt.error.headerNotObject: The header must be a JSON object.
tool.jwt.error.incomplete: Not a complete JWT: it needs at least two parts separated by a dot.
tool.jwt.error.jwe: This is a JWE (5 parts): its payload is encrypted, so there is nothing to decode without the key.
tool.jwt.error.keyBadJson: The key looks like JSON but does not parse. Paste a JWK or a PEM.
tool.jwt.error.keyMismatch: That key cannot verify {alg} ({reason}). Check the key type: RS/PS need RSA, ES256/384/512 need a P-256/384/521 EC key, EdDSA needs Ed25519.
tool.jwt.error.keyNotObject: Paste a JWK object or a PEM public key.
tool.jwt.error.needsPublicKey: {alg} needs the issuer's public key: paste a PEM or JWK in the Public key option.
tool.jwt.error.noSignature: This token has no signature part, so there is nothing to crack.
tool.jwt.error.noWebCrypto: WebCrypto is not available here (it needs HTTPS or localhost). HS256/384/512 still work.
tool.jwt.error.notFound: No JWT found. A token is three Base64URL parts joined by dots and starting with "eyJ", e.g. eyJhbGciOi….eyJzdWIi….signature.
tool.jwt.error.notHmac: Cracking only applies to HMAC tokens (HS256/384/512); this one uses {alg}. For RS/ES tokens there is no shared secret to guess.
tool.jwt.error.partCount_one: A JWT has 3 parts separated by dots, this one has {count}.
tool.jwt.error.partCount_other: A JWT has 3 parts separated by dots, this one has {count}.
tool.jwt.error.payloadNotB64: The payload is not Base64URL ({reason}) Was the token cut short?
tool.jwt.error.pemLabel: Unsupported PEM block "{label}". Use "PUBLIC KEY" (SPKI) or a JWK.
tool.jwt.error.privateKey: That is a private key. Verifying only needs the public half: openssl pkey -in key.pem -pubout
tool.jwt.error.signBadJson: The input starts like JSON but does not parse. Check quotes and commas.
tool.jwt.error.signEmpty: Paste a token to re-sign, or JSON like {"user":"admin"}.
tool.jwt.error.signNeedsSecret: {alg} needs a secret: fill the Secret option.
tool.jwt.error.signPayloadNotJson: That token's payload is not JSON, so it cannot be re-signed here.
tool.jwt.error.signatureNotB64: The signature is not Base64URL ({reason}) Was the token cut short?
tool.jwt.error.unreadableKey: Could not read the public key. Paste a PEM ("-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----…"), a JWK or a JWKS.
tool.jwt.error.unsupportedAlg: Unsupported alg "{alg}". Supported: HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, EdDSA.
tool.jwt.error.verifyNeedsSecret: {alg} needs the secret: fill the Secret option (or use Crack mode).
tool.jwt.error.verifyNoAlg: The header has no "alg", so there is no way to know how to verify.
tool.jwt.label.spellings: Spellings to try against a filter that blocks "none"
tool.jwt.meaning.badExp: exp is not a valid timestamp
tool.jwt.meaning.millis: looks like milliseconds, JWT expects seconds
tool.jwt.meaning.notSeconds: should be a number of seconds since 1970
tool.jwt.name: JWT
tool.jwt.note.algNone: alg is "{alg}": this token is unsigned. If the server accepts it, any payload can be forged. Try Sign mode with alg none (the tool also prints the None/NONE/nOnE spellings).
tool.jwt.note.asymmetric: {alg} is asymmetric. Worth testing: sign the token as HS256 using the server's public key as the HMAC secret (algorithm confusion), or alg none.
tool.jwt.note.emptySecret: The secret is the empty string.
tool.jwt.note.forge: Switch to Sign mode with this secret to forge a token (change the role, user or exp claims).
tool.jwt.note.jku: jku is set ({value}): the server may fetch keys from this URL. Check whether it validates the host.
tool.jwt.note.jwk: jwk is embedded in the header: a server that trusts it lets you sign with your own key (CVE-2018-0114 style).
tool.jwt.note.kid: kid is set ({value}): the server uses it to pick a key. Test path traversal (../../dev/null with an empty secret), SQL injection and command injection in this value.
tool.jwt.note.mismatchKey: Signature does NOT match ({alg}) with this key.
tool.jwt.note.mismatchSecret: Signature does NOT match ({alg}) with this secret. Wrong secret, or try "Secret is Base64"; Crack mode tests common weak secrets.
tool.jwt.note.noAlg: The header has no "alg". Servers differ in how they handle that.
tool.jwt.note.noMatch_one: None of the {count} candidates matches. Add guesses in "Extra candidates", or go offline: hashcat -m 16500 token.txt wordlist.txt
tool.jwt.note.noMatch_other: None of the {count} candidates matches. Add guesses in "Extra candidates", or go offline: hashcat -m 16500 token.txt wordlist.txt
tool.jwt.note.noneNoSignature: alg is "{alg}": there is no signature to verify. Servers that accept this are vulnerable.
tool.jwt.note.noneWithSignature: alg is "{alg}" but the token carries a signature. A compliant server rejects "none" tokens outright.
tool.jwt.note.payloadNotObject: The payload is not a JSON object, so there are no claims to list.
tool.jwt.note.weakSecret: Weak secret found: this token is signed with "{secret}". Anyone can forge tokens: use Sign mode.
tool.jwt.note.x5c: x5c is embedded in the header: a server that trusts it lets you sign with your own certificate.
tool.jwt.note.x5u: x5u is set ({value}): the server may fetch a certificate from this URL. Check whether it validates the host.
